newsitem.title: USA: Duke says large block sold by pension fund.
newsitem.headline: Duke says large block sold by pension fund.

text.p: Shares in Duke Realty Inc slipped 5/8 to 32-1/2 on more than 10 times normal trading volume on Friday morning after the sale at 31 of a large block by a British pension fund, the company said.

"We don't think they sold due to any fundamental reason having to do with the company. And we don't know why they sold in one block," said Thomas Peck, spokesman for Duke, an Indianapolis-based commercial real estate investment trust. "On the surface, it seems like they could have done a little better if they had dribbled it out some."

Peck declined to identify the pension fund, but said that it sold 605,000 shares that it had obtained in recent months by converting operating partnership units it held following Duke's 1993 public offering.
Duke has about 29 million common shares and four million operating partnership units outstanding, he said.
Duke's typical daily trading volume is 60,000 to 70,000 shares. On Friday morning, volume was 772,900 shares.
Institutions own about 45 percent of Duke's stock. About 12 percent is owned by insiders and the balance is in the retail market, Peck said.
The company's properties encompass more than 25 million rentable square feet and are located in Indianapolis, Cincinnati, Cleveland, St. Louis, Nashville, Tenn., and Columbus, Ohio.
